newsitem.title: ITALY: AGIP PLANS TO LOWER PETROL PRICES - ENI HEAD.
newsitem.headline: AGIP PLANS TO LOWER PETROL PRICES - ENI HEAD.

text.p: Italian state oil company Agip SpA plans to lower its petrol pump price as early as Monday, Eni managing director Franco Bernabe said in an interview published on Sunday.
"On Monday we will make our assessments and if there are no more hikes in the dollar rate, we will reduce the price of petrol," Bernabe told Il Corriere della Sera newspaper.
Agip is a unit of state energy giant Eni.
Bernabe did not indicate how much the reduction would be, and warned the fall would not necessarily be long-term.
"Iraqi oil should be back on the market by the end of the month and we will immediately make the first buys," Bernabe said.

Italy's oil industry body, Unione Petrolifera (UP), agreed last week to an eight-day price freeze after member companies came under fire by the government for hiking pump tariffs in response to recent dollar gains.
The prices between the distributors varied between 1,930-1,935 lire per litre of leaded petrol and 1,840-1,845 lire for a litre of unleaded petrol.
A weakening of the dollar on Friday gave reason to believe prices would fall again.
"The signs we are seeing from the dollar and from crude oil are positive for (a drop in) petrol prices," UP president Pasquale de Vita said on Saturday.
